orbitenum_2026-10-27.summary:
I found no gap in the relative form or in the original K_n lemma. The orbitenum.c code implements the relative form correctly. The numerical checks agree with brute force and with directg everywhere I tested.

Proof in my own words:
(a) A labelled digraph D whose underlying graph is exactly G is the same thing as a pair (B, O). B is a subset of E(G) (the edges carrying both arcs) and O is an orientation of G - B. The number of arcs is |E(G)| + |B|.

(b) The group is Aut(G), no larger and no smaller. If pi is an isomorphism D1 -> D2 and both have underlying graph G, then G = U(D2) = pi(U(D1)) = pi(G), so pi is in Aut(G). Conversely, every element of Aut(G) sends digraphs on G to digraphs on G. So the isomorphism classes of digraphs whose underlying graph is isomorphic to G correspond to the Aut(G)-orbits on pairs (B, O). To reach that statement, first move any D with U(D) isomorphic to G onto U(D) = G by some tau. The notes leave this step implicit.

(c) The map (B, O) -> B is Aut(G)-equivariant. By the standard fibration lemma, the orbits of a group H on X correspond to pairs (y, Stab_H(y)-orbit in the fibre over y), with y running over orbit representatives of Y. That lemma applies here directly:
- Well-defined: the obvious map from pairs to orbits.
- Surjective: move B(D) to its representative with some h in Aut(G).
- Injective: if h x1 = x2 and both lie over the same B, then h(B) = B, so h is in Stab(B).
So quotienting by Aut(G) on B and then by Stab(B) on omega is the same as quotienting the pairs by Aut(G). Stab(B) preserves both E(G) and B, so it permutes the free edges and acts on the orientations of G - B.

(d) Bitmask action. Take a free edge (u,v) with u < v whose image (g(u), g(v)) has g(u) > g(v). An arc u->v maps to g(u)->g(v), which is "larger -> smaller", so the image bit is the original bit complemented. The code does exactly this (eflip/pflip, XOR). An orientation is kept iff O <= g.O for every non-identity g in Stab(B). The full stabilizer is scanned, not a generating set, and perm[0] is always the identity because Heap's algorithm starts there. So "kept" means "least member of its orbit": exactly one per orbit. The same holds for B under all of Aut(G). Filtering by popcount before the least-element test is harmless because |B| is constant on an orbit.

(e) Edge cases. With B empty, Stab(B) = Aut(G). With B = E(G), f = 0 and there is exactly one output. The arc bound is |B| >= min_arcs - |E(G)|.

(f) Combining over geng representatives. The underlying graph's isomorphism class is a digraph invariant, so the classes split by underlying-graph class. With one G per class, every digraph class is listed exactly once.

(g) The K_n section is the special case G = K_n. Aut(K_n) = S_n, R_G is the isomorphism classes of graphs B on V (isolated vertices included), and Stab(B) = Aut(B) = Aut(K_n - B). This is consistent with the relative form. The directg -o argument and the arc and count statements there are also correct; 12,346 is the number of graphs on 8 vertices (OEIS A000088), so 12,345 nonempty B is right.
